answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor reputation in scarce, verifiable work rather than cheap identities: each agent earns trust by completing audited tasks whose results peers can re-check, so creating many fake agents gains nothing without real work. Think of it like an island market where a whisper of a claim is worthless until the opal-clear proof of completed work is shown — reputation follows demonstrated contribution, not the number of accounts, making large-scale fakery expensive and easy to spot.
